title: Vanadium(IV)-chlorodipicolinate alleviates hepatic steatosis via the AMPK/PGC-1alpha/CPT1a axis.
authors: Chen, Rulong; Liu, Yufan; Wang, Yuanli; Zhang, Fang; Ma, Jinkui; Cui, Wei; Ding, Wenjun
journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
one_liner_zh: 该文研究钒化合物通过AMPK/PGC-1alpha/CPT1a通路改善肝脏脂肪变性，虽涉及分子动力学模拟，但核心是代谢调控而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is closely associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is characterized by hepatic steatosis. Vanadium compounds have the potential to prevent hyperlipidemia. However, whether vanadium compound supplementation could rescue hepatic steatosis in NAFLD remains uncertain. We sought to investigate the molecular mechanisms by which vanadium(IV)-chlorodipicolinate (VOdipic-Cl) ameliorated hepatic steatosis in obesity. The therapeutic effect of VOdipic-Cl was evaluated using high-fat diet (HFD)-induced C57BL/6 mice and palmitic acid/oleic acid (PO)-treated L02 hepatocytes, respectively. Lipidomic analysis, RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq), Western blotting, and molecular dynamics simulation were employed to elucidate the molecular mechanism of VOdipic-Cl in regulating lipid metabolism in liver and hepatocytes. VOdipic-Cl treatment effectively reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and improved hepatic function in HFD-fed mice. Lipidomic analysis showed that the primary differential lipid metabolites were mainly associated with glycerophospholipid metabolism pathway. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling pathway was involved in the regulation of hepatic lipid metabolism by VOdipic-Cl treatment. Moreover, VOdipic-Cl-induced AMPK activation significantly restored hepatic mitochondrial homeostasis and reduced lipid accumulation through upregulating transcription factor peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator-1alpha (PGC-1alpha) and carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 (CPT1) in hepatocytes, respectively. Our findings suggest that VOdipic-Cl triggers the activation of AMPK, leading to the upregulation of PGC-1alpha and CPT1 expression, ultimately improving mitochondrial homeostasis and decreasing lipid accumulation. Collectively, these molecular cascades contribute to the ameliorating effect of VOdipic-Cl on HFD-induced hepatic steatosis. This study also provides evidence supporting the potential utilization of VOdipic-Cl for the treatment of NAFLD.
abstract_zh: 非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）与以肝脂肪变性为特征的2型糖尿病密切相关。钒化合物具有预防高脂血症的潜力。然而，钒化合物补充剂是否能缓解NAFLD中的肝脂肪变性仍不确定。我们旨在研究钒(IV)-氯二吡啶甲酸（VOdipic-Cl）改善肥胖中肝脂肪变性的分子机制。分别使用高脂饮食（HFD）诱导的C57BL/6小鼠和棕榈酸/油酸（PO）处理的L02肝细胞评估VOdipic-Cl的治疗效果。采用脂质组学分析、RNA测序（RNA-seq）、Western blotting和分子动力学模拟来阐明VOdipic-Cl在调节肝脏和肝细胞脂质代谢中的分子机制。VOdipic-Cl处理有效减少了HFD喂养小鼠的肝脏脂质积累并改善了肝功能。脂质组学分析显示，主要差异脂质代谢物主要与甘油磷脂代谢途径相关。转录组学分析揭示，腺苷酸活化蛋白激酶（AMPK）信号通路参与了VOdipic-Cl处理对肝脏脂质代谢的调节。此外，VOdipic-Cl诱导的AMPK激活通过分别上调肝细胞中转录因子过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ共激活因子-1α（PGC-1alpha）和肉碱棕榈酰转移酶1（CPT1）的表达，显著恢复线粒体稳态并减少脂质积累。我们的研究结果表明，VOdipic-Cl触发AMPK的激活，导致PGC-1alpha和CPT1表达上调，最终改善线粒体稳态并减少脂质积累。总体而言，这些分子级联反应有助于VOdipic-Cl对HFD诱导的肝脂肪变性的改善作用。本研究还为VOdipic-Cl在NAFLD治疗中的潜在应用提供了证据支持。
